message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of some of the most acclaimed crime‑thriller releases from 2020 (in no particular order):

| # | Title | Director | Notable Cast | Why It Stands Out |
|---|-------|----------|--------------|-------------------|
| 1 | **The Invisible Man** | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss, Oliver Jackson-Cohen | A modern take on the classic horror trope with strong psychological tension and a standout performance by Moss. |
| 2 | **Tenet** | Christopher Nolan | John David Washington, Robert Pattinson | Nolan’s signature time‑bending narrative combined with high‑concept action sequences. |
| 3 | **The Gentlemen** | Guy Ritchie | Matthew McConaughey, Charlie Hunnam, Hugh Grant | Ritchie’s sharp dialogue and stylish heist plot delivered a fresh comedic edge to the genre. |
| 4 | **The Trial of the Chicago 7** | Aaron Sorkin | Eddie Redmayne, Sacha Baron Cohen | A courtroom drama that blends political intrigue with a compelling ensemble cast. |
| 5 | **Uncut Gems** | Ben Safdie & Joshua Safdie | Adam Sandler, Kevin Garnett | Sandler’s manic performance anchors a tense, high‑stakes thriller about addiction and risk. |
| 6 | **The Hunt** | Thomas Vinterberg | Mads Mikkelsen, Nikolaj Coster-Waldau | A harrowing look at social media paranoia and moral panic, featuring powerful performances. |
| 7 | **The Irishman** | Martin Scorsese | Robert De Niro, Al Pacino, Joe Pesci | Scorsese’s epic saga of organized crime, shot in de‑aged CGI, offers a reflective, long‑form narrative. |
| 8 | **The Little Things** | John Lee Hancock | Denzel Washington, Rami Malek, Jared Leto | A gritty, atmospheric mystery that explores the psychological toll of obsession. |
| 9 | **The Night House** | David Bruckner | Rebecca Hall, Nathan Lane | A psychological thriller that blends supernatural elements with domestic suspense. |
|10 | **The Platform** | Galder Gaztelu-Urrutia | Iván Massagué, Zorion Eguileor | A Spanish allegory that uses a vertical prison setting to explore class conflict and survival. |

These films showcase a range of styles—from high‑concept sci‑fi thrillers to grounded, character‑driven dramas—making them worth checking out if you’re into crime‑thrillers.
